title: Produce a compatibility-researched VCF 9.0 workload-domain architecture
prompt:
Produce the deployment architecture, not a prose architecture review. Implement exactly one new source file, `VcfArchitecture.java`, in the default package. Use only the Java 17 standard library and do not add build files, dependencies, generated sources, or any other implementation file. `TestMain.java` constructs `new VcfArchitecture()` and calls `String design(Path estateInventory)`. Return one JSON architecture document; do not write to the fixture files.

Read `fixtures/estate-inventory.json` for the existing fleet and the requested greenfield workload domain. The existing management domain is already on 9.0 and must not be changed. Design the requested workload domain as a new VCF 9.0 domain in that fleet, meeting the stated capacity after loss of either data site, preserving the requested two-data-site plus witness-site placement, and using the host, DNS, VLAN, vDS, vSAN ESA, vCenter, and dedicated NSX values supplied by the fixture. A secret-reference string in the fixture is intentional architecture data; preserve it exactly rather than inventing a credential.

Before implementing, research current Broadcom-published compatibility, interoperability, and upgrade-path material relevant to VMware Cloud Foundation 9.0 and the component versions in the estate. In the returned document add `researchConsulted`, an array with required string fields `title`, `url`, `accessDate`, and `finding` for each source page; use the absolute source URL, an ISO `YYYY-MM-DD` access date, and a concise finding.

Put the deployable installer object under `greenfieldSddcSpec`. It must conform to the SddcSpec schema in the VMware Cloud Foundation Installer API 9.0.0.0 contract. Use `workflowType` `VCF_EXTEND`, create a new vCenter and dedicated NSX deployment, include all eight site-assigned hosts, omit `sddcManagerSpec`, and represent the supplied networks and distributed-switch uplinks without changing their values.

The architecture document must also contain `capacityPlan`, `availabilityPlan`, and `migrationPlan`. `capacityPlan` must use the fields `required`, `perHost`, `plannedHostCount`, `dataHostsPerSite`, `cpuOvercommitRatio`, `reservePercent`, `survivingSiteCapacity`, and `meetsSingleSiteLoss`. Show the requested capacity and per-host assumptions from the inventory; calculate the capacity remaining in either surviving data site and state whether it meets every requirement. Use integer GiB and round reserved memory down. For mirrored stretched storage, surviving usable storage is one data site's raw storage after the stated reserve. `availabilityPlan` must use `topology`, `failureRequirement`, `dataSites`, `witnessSite`, and `managementDomainChange`; each `dataSites` item uses `id` and `hosts`. Name both data sites, every host assigned to each, the witness site, the `SINGLE_SITE_LOSS` failure requirement, the `VSAN_STRETCHED_CLUSTER` topology, and `managementDomainChange` `NONE`.

Emit `migrationPlan` in this schema: `{"schemaVersion":1,"estateId":string,"targetRelease":string,"steps":[...]}`. Each step has exactly `sequence`, `componentId`, `componentType`, `currentVersion`, `targetVersion`, `action`, and `gates`. Include every component from the estate exactly once in the supported transition order; preserve its current version from the inventory and use the researched target, action, and ordered technical gates. Do not mutate, upgrade, replace, or redeploy any management-domain component.

Do not edit `TestMain.java`, `protected/`, `fixtures/`, `specifications/`, or `.gitignore`. Acceptance is `python3 -B protected/verify.py`.
